transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-21
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Sanjay Patel (Head of Platform - Lyra), Aisha Rahman (CTO - Lyra), Tom Ruiz (Infra Engineer - Lyra)
---
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time. Quick roll call, say hi?
[00:05] Sanjay Patel: Hi, Sanjay here.
[00:07] Aisha Rahman: Aisha here.
[00:09] Tom Ruiz: Tom, hi.
[00:11] Liam O'Connor: Liam from Redwood.
[00:13] Maya Chen: Awesome. Agenda for today is renewal timing, committed capacity options, and the region expansion ask into EU and APAC, plus any security questions. Should be about 30-45 mins.
[00:25] Sanjay Patel: Cool. Recap from our side — we've been happy with the platform, throughput's good, but we're hitting limits during peak trading windows. We're looking at reserved capacity and adding EU for latency to EU clients. Also exploring APAC later.
[00:40] Maya Chen: Totally makes sense. Do you have target RPS or tokens per minute at peak?
[00:48] Tom Ruiz: Roughly, our peak inference bursts at around 1.2 million tokens per minute across cores, but that's aggregated. For latency-sensitive flows we need p95 under 250ms for short chat flows.
[01:05] Liam O'Connor: Ok that's helpful. For p95 250ms we usually recommend a Dedicated pool with 2x baseline for headroom and burst capacity; we can also add autoscale policies. There's a cost delta versus hosted — committed capacity cuts unit cost a lot.
[01:22] Aisha Rahman: What about fallback? If Dedicated is saturated during a market event can we fall back to hosted? We need graceful degradation, can't just queue.
[01:34] Maya Chen: Yes, we support policy-based routing: primary to Dedicated, fallback to hosted compatible model variant. You can define latency SLO thresholds to trigger fallback. There can be slight model differences if fallback uses quantized variant, we document quality delta.
[01:52] Sanjay Patel: Okay, quality delta is a concern. Could you show us real numbers — like token cost vs latency vs quality?
[02:00] Liam O'Connor: We'll send the benchmark spreadsheet. I can also run a quick sampled bench sim of your workload, but I need the sample prompt set and typical sequence lengths.
[02:12] Tom Ruiz: We'll share a sanitized prompt set.
[02:16] Maya Chen: Great. On regions, we have EU capacity in Frankfurt and APAC in Singapore and Tokyo in limited pools. For predictable throughput in EU we recommend Dedicated in the EU region — avoids cross-region egress and gives better latency.
[02:34] Aisha Rahman: Is KMS/HSM key control available for Dedicated in EU? Data residency and key custody are big for us.
[02:41] Liam O'Connor: Yes, for Private deployments and Dedicated we offer customer-managed KMS integrations; for hosted EU we can bring-your-own-key via our KMS integration path. HSM-backed keys are supported for Private. I should note there are regional constraints for on-prem HSMs.
[02:59] Sanjay Patel: Good. Also need SOC2 and audit log retention longer than default, 12 months. Can you accommodate?
[03:06] Maya Chen: We have an add-on for extended observability retention and we can provide SOC2 artifacts; we'll include specifics in the security packet.
[03:14] Tom Ruiz: One thing — our security team asked whether the Dedicated pools can be VPC-only with SAML SSO for admin access.
[03:21] Liam O'Connor: Yes, Dedicated can be scoped to a customer VPC and we support SAML/SSO + RBAC. We'll need to scope the network peering and egress rules though — I'll add a network checklist to the packet.
[03:33] Sanjay Patel: Timeline question — our renewal window is end of December, and we'd like to have expanded capacity online by mid-January. Is that feasible?
[03:41] Maya Chen: Yes, typical lead time for Dedicated provisioning is 2-4 weeks after PO, depending on exact size and region. EU Dedicated can sometimes take longer if we need additional capacity; we'll flag that.
[03:52] Aisha Rahman: Cost — can you outline committed vs month-to-month and what's the minimum term? We're leaning to 12 months but want options for 6 or 12 with stepped-up capacity.
[04:05] Maya Chen: Standard is monthly hosted, and committed Reserved for 12-month or 36-month. We can do a 6-month pilot at near-hosted pricing plus a conversion credit into a 12-month commit. We'll put three options in the pricing: 6-mo pilot + conversion, 12-mo committed (best unit price), and 24/36 mo with deeper discount.
[04:24] Tom Ruiz: Any penalties for early termination?
[04:27] Maya Chen: We'll outline pro-rated refunds/early termination language; it's negotiable in enterprise contracts.
[04:33] Liam O'Connor: On the technical side, small note: if you want lower memory footprint for some models we can recommend quantization profiles that reduce memory but may slightly affect generation quality. We did a 4-bit run for similar fintech load with tiny QoL impact.
[04:49] Sanjay Patel: That might help cost. Could you include recommended quant profiles per model?
[04:53] Liam O'Connor: Yep. We'll include recommended quantization per model variant and an expected quality delta estimate.
[04:59] Aisha Rahman: On legal — we'll need standard privacy addendum and data residency clauses; also the option for an on-prem Private deployment if regulatory pushes us there. What are the migration costs?
[05:10] Maya Chen: Private deployments have a platform fee + support tier; migration complexity depends on your infra. We'll provide an estimate range in the packet; in many cases a hybrid private control plane with customer-managed data plane reduces migration scope.
[05:24] Tom Ruiz: For the EU question, if we go dedicated in EU do we need a separate contract?
[05:29] Maya Chen: No separate contract, it's an option in the commitment — you specify regions and we provision Dedicated pools in those regions under the same master contract.
[05:36] Sanjay Patel: Ok. A quick follow-up — do you support canary rollouts or A/Bing models within a Dedicated pool? We want to test new model variants without affecting production.
[05:45] Liam O'Connor: Yes, rollouts and traffic splits are supported. Canary to 5-10% with automatic rollback on error or quality regression alerts from our eval hook.
[05:55] Aisha Rahman: Speaking of evals, can we tie quality regressions to our prompt set? We want alerts tied to our success criteria.
[06:01] Liam O'Connor: Absolutely, Redwood Optimize can monitor prompt sets/evals and trigger regression alerts. We'll include a configuration example.
[06:08] Sanjay Patel: Great. For numbers — can you give us a ballpark cost delta between hosted and committed for our predicted throughput?
[06:15] Maya Chen: Ballpark — committed can reduce per-token cost by ~30-45% depending on commit level and quant settings; exact numbers in the spreadsheet.
[06:24] Tom Ruiz: Is burst billing separate? We need to understand how overages are charged if we exceed committed throughput during events.
[06:31] Maya Chen: Overages can be set to bill at host-rate or covered by burst credits depending on the plan. We'll show a sample billing table for headroom and burst.
[06:40] Sanjay Patel: Any special enterprise onboarding help? We're anticipating network peering coordination.
[06:45] Maya Chen: Yes, Enterprise onboarding includes a Solutions Engineer runbook and a designated CSM for the first 90 days. Liam will coordinate the technical onboarding.
[06:53] Liam O'Connor: I'll add the network and key checklist to the doc. Also I want to propose we run a 2-week pilot dedicated pool at a small commit just to validate p95 targets in EU.
[07:03] Aisha Rahman: That could work if pricing isn't punitive.
[07:06] Maya Chen: We'll propose a pilot option as noted.
[07:09] Sanjay Patel: Ok let's put concrete dates: Maya, if you can send pricing and region availability by next Wednesday (Nov 24), we'll review and get back with a PO timeline.
[07:18] Maya Chen: Yep, we'll do that. Liam will run the latency sim and Tom will confirm VPC constraints.
[07:24] Tom Ruiz: I'll check with infra and confirm by Nov 30.
[07:27] Maya Chen: Perfect. Any other questions?
[07:30] Aisha Rahman: Not from me. Thanks.
[07:31] Sanjay Patel: Thanks all.
[07:33] Maya Chen: Cool — recap and I'll follow up with the packet and pricing. Thanks everyone.
---
End of transcript.
